title: EXCLUSIVE: Marcos confronted Romualdez over insertions that would have laid off 7,000 DPWH staff --Bonoan
summary: Pres. Marcos Jr. confronted then-House Speaker Romualdez over the near-layoff of some 7,000 daily wage employees of the DPWH due to congressional insertions in 2024, Manuel Bonoan said.

blocks.text: Published November 23, 2026 8:01pm

President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. confronted then-House Speaker Martin Romualdez over the near-layoff of some 7,000 daily wage employees of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) due to congressional insertions in 2024, former DPWH secretary Manuel Bonoan stated in a judicial affidavit exclusively obtained by GMA News.

Bonoan said the DPWH was cash-strapped after legislators took the budget allotted for its Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE) to allocate it to more than 9,000 congressional insertions worth P 380.48 billion.
Legislators also took the more than P70.701 billion allocated for infrastructure projects or foreign-assisted projects like the Metro Manila Subway Project or the North South Rail Commuter Project.
“… the legislators took everything leaving nothing for the IFP/FAP,” Bonoan said.
Bonoan said the President immediately called Romualdez after he had informed him about this.

“The President was so concerned about laying off 7,000 DPWH daily wage employees, so he immediately called [then-] Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez in my presence. To my recollection, the President told Speaker Martin, ‘Ano ba naman kayo, magtatanggal si Secretary Manny ng 7,000 employees dahil kinuha n’yo pati MOOE n’ya. Hindi pwede ito,” he said.
Bonoan said Romualdez reprimanded him for reporting to the President..
“Sometime after that Speaker Martin Romualdez called me up and told me ‘Pambihira ka naman Sec., pwede ka namang dumeretso sa akin, nagsumbong ka pa kay Presidente,” Bonoan recounted.
Bonoan told Romualdez that the President was his boss.
But despite the President’s warning, it continued even in the 2025 budget.

“Notwithstanding the phone call of the President, the House Of Representatives and the Senate of the Philippines still slashed the Department’s proposed budget for the Fiscal Year 2025 to fund their ‘congressional initiatives’ or ‘insertions,” Bonoan said.
In 2025, there was some P436 billion in congressional insertions according to Bonoan which irked the President that he wanted to veto the whole 2025 budget.
“The President was furious that he wanted to veto the entire 2025 GAB but his economic managers advised the President not to,” Bonoan said.

The President then instructed Bonoan to identify which projects he could veto and Bonoan identified some P26 billion pesos of infrastructure projects which he called “guni-guni” projects that included highways in mountains that run to legislators’ resorts.

“These projects I recommended to be vetoed are ambiguous or ‘guni-guni’ projects that I reported to the President. These projects were construction of highways to the mountains leading to resorts of legislators, construction of new buildings, hostels and swimming pools, etc. These projects are not aligned with the core programs of the government,” Bonoan said.

Of the P400 billion in insertions, P192 billion came from the House of Representatives while some P17 billion were “jointly tagged under the names of both senators and members of the House of Representatives.”
Bonoan furnished the court with a listing of Romualdez alleged insertions including that of former House Committee on Appropriations Chair Zaldy Co.
A GMA News source said Romualdez’ amount of insertions is around P27 billion.
GMA News sought the Romualdez and Co’s comments but their counsels refused comment. — BM, GMA News
